full_allotment.rule: the facility is at full allotment on target day T when the `standing_repo` entry of metadata/policy_events.json in force on T (the latest effective date on or before T, then the latest announcement, among the entries announced at or before the decision instant) states no aggregate operation limit: details.aggregate_operation_limit_bn is null. The first such entry is `standing_repo-20251210` (announced 2025-12-10 14:00, effective 2025-12-11). An entry without the field is refused (ValueError), never read as full allotment
full_allotment.no_date_in_code: no date is hard-coded. An entry that re-imposes an aggregate limit stops the cap on its effective date; one that removes it again restarts it; tests/test_s3c_candidate.py tests both directions on a synthetic register
full_allotment.information_set: the entry read is the one repo_model.srf_line reads for the line: announced at or before the decision instant (16:00 America/New_York on the decision day, the published records' decision time) and effective on or before T, passed through policy_events.require_announced, which raises LookAheadError for an entry announced later. This is the availability rule of metadata/srf_cap_1241.json (scheduled_availability, basis announced_before_ref_date, 1 business day, 16:00), unchanged
full_allotment.later_entry: metadata/policy_events.json also holds `standing_repo-20260916` (announced 2026-09-16, effective 2026-09-17; no aggregate limit). It is after the last scored day (2026-09-03) and after the panel's build cutoff, and is not read by any scored cell

scoring.scorer: repo_model.scoring_protocol (#655), the development tier: no verdict, no registration
scoring.test: scoring_protocol.paired_tests, the studentized stationary bootstrap (ruling 1), mean block 10 business days, 10,000 draws, seed 1255, two-sided 90% interval (the lower end is the one-sided 95% bound); both the skill interval and the studentized interval on mean d (bp) are reported for every tested row; where the studentized bound cannot be computed (most of a group's days score alike) the unstudentized percentile interval of mean d is given beside, with no reading taken from it
scoring.reading: a reading is taken from the mean-d bound (Eleonora's ruling on #1009, 20 October 2026): (s3c) is read better than a reference when the lower end of the 90% interval of mean d is above zero, worse when the upper end is below zero, otherwise undecided. The skill interval's reading is listed beside it where it differs. Lens C's caveat (the lag-10 HAC standard error is understated about 2x after 2020) is stated on the page
scoring.politis_white: the Politis-White block of the paired differential against (s3) is reported for the pooled group, as #1241 reported it
scoring.identical_groups: a group in which (s3c)'s score equals (s3)'s on every day is listed as identical against (s3) and not tested against it; a group of fewer than 20 days is listed and not tested
scoring.day_type_intervals: the intervals of a pressure-day-type, calendar-day-type or month group keep the current method (the group's days, scattered, resampled in date order as if consecutive), which #1221 questions and #1228 will decide; the page labels them so and reads no pressure-day type from them

reading_rules: A figure is a check on days that were already seen. Nothing here is a verdict, nothing is registered and no choice is made on it.

A gain of (s3c) over a reference is read as present on a split when the 90% interval of mean d excludes zero on the positive side, and as a loss when it excludes zero on the negative side; otherwise as undecided. A point estimate alone is not read.

A pooled figure is never read without the regime (development window) or month (2026) and pressure-day-type splits beside it. The upper-tail figures of the 2026 window rest on few pressure days; the page states the counts.
Lens C's caveat is stated on the page. The day-type and month intervals are labelled as the current method (#1221 open, #1228).
